title: Screening electrode materials for scaling tubular electrochemical flow systems
content: Tubular vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) offer competitive advantages distinct from conventional planar architectures, including the potential for higher packing efficiency and lower stack costs for scalable energy storage. However, their operation is constrained by high polarization arising from long electron-transfer pathways in tubular geometries. Here, we combined analytical screening and electrochemical characterization to identify Cu as a promising alternative to graphite anodes for tubular VRFBs. Compared to graphite, Cu exhibits more reversible V2+/V3+ redox behavior and lower ohmic and kinetic polarization. These advantages lead to higher electrolyte utilization and improved cycling efficiency in Cu-based tubular VRFBs. Moreover, Cu's high electrical conductivity and ductility support scalable fabrication of tubular electrodes while providing broader design flexibility. Beyond demonstrating Cu as a viable anode candidate for tubular VRFBs, this work also establishes a material-selection framework for evaluating electrode materials in tubular electrochemical flow architectures that require longer, thinner, and more compact designs.
